<reason>A won a competitive debate by making the choice easier: tax privileges are a function-based public bargain, not a unique PAC subsidy. B’s honest concession that even a congregation spending most of its budget on nominee turnout still keeps deductibility and property-tax relief left CON with no off-ramp. A’s operational primary-purpose test and PAC-split answer handled the theology and pantry objections more cleanly than B answered the loophole and election-law inconsistency. B’s church-state and enforcement warnings stayed live but did not neutralize the motion.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s Q1 forced B to keep full tax advantages even for a majority-campaign church; A then used that concession as the decisive comparative in rebuttal 2 and closing.</best_rebuttal>
